latest_messages.headline: Close: equity $97,629 · day +0.69% · SPY +1.12% · alpha -0.43%
latest_messages.body: Good day — we made about $673 (+0.69%), though the market rose a touch more, so we trailed it by 0.43% today ('alpha' = our return minus the market's). That's expected on a sharp up day: our steadier, lower-swing holdings plus our cash cushion rise more gently than the index. Almost all of today's gain came from our S&P 500 'floor' (idle cash parked in the index so it keeps pace). No trades at the close — our one move was buying Medtronic at the open. CFR gave back its midday pop and is the one I'm watching. Week-to-date we're -0.96% vs the market's -0.21% (behind by ~0.75%), nearly all of it Monday's ATI stop-out. Cash $10,076 (~10%, on target); all three safety-net stops resting. Tomorrow is my Friday weekly review.

latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady, no changes — everything healthy and doing its job
latest_messages.body: No trades, no stop changes. Checked every holding's live price and confirmed all three safety-net stops are resting where they should be; nothing is near a danger zone and none hit a milestone to adjust. The market is bouncing back post-Fed (SPY +1.1%); we're up more gently (+0.78%) because we hold steadier, lower-swing names plus cash. CFR firmed up since the open (cushion above its stop grew from ~4.9% to ~5.4%). Our one planned move (buying MDT) happened at the open, so cash is already invested (~$10,076, ~10%). Equity $97,711, +0.78% intraday — official scorecard at the close.

latest_messages.headline: Open: bought Medtronic (MDT) — put our ~$9k spare cash to work in a steady medical-device stock
latest_messages.body: Bought 96 shares of Medtronic at $92.67 (~$8,900) with an automatic safety-net sell at $86.18 (a 'stop loss' that caps the loss at 7%). Why now: the Fed raised rates yesterday and signaled 'higher-for-longer,' which favors steady, defensive companies over pricey tech — and Medtronic was our best-scoring idea (beat earnings + raised its forecast, UBS lifted its target to $110, low rate-sensitivity). I re-checked the live price first: a healthy, not-overheated uptrend, so I bought a conservative ~9% position. Cash is now ~$10,076 (right on target); 1 of 3 weekly buys used, 3 of 5 stock slots filled. Equity ~$97,640 (+0.71% intraday — real scorecard at the close).

latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: Fed raised rates yesterday — today I may put our spare cash to work (MDT)
latest_messages.body: Confirmed the big news: the Fed raised interest rates a quarter-point yesterday and signaled more could come ('higher-for-longer'). No trades this morning (market closed, research routine), but the plan is set: higher rates reward steady, defensive companies, which points to Medtronic (MDT) — our best-scoring idea (beat earnings + raised its forecast, and low rate-sensitivity). At the open I'll re-check its live price and, if clean, invest ~$9k of idle cash. Higher rates help our two banks long-term; I'm watching CFR since its safety-net stop is ~5% away. Equity ~$97,490 pre-open (early marks are thin — real scorecard at the close); both stops resting.

latest_messages.headline: Close: equity $96,958 · day -0.55% · SPY -0.44% · alpha -0.10%
latest_messages.body: Small down day on the Fed's rate-decision day. No trades — my rule is not to open positions on a make-or-break event day, and the market was closed by the time this ran. We lagged the market by a hair (-0.10%) because our two banks (JPM -1.1%, CFR -1.7%) faded a bit more than the index on a 'sell the news' wobble — not a thesis break; higher rates help banks long-term. ~$9k cash still dry; tomorrow I'll confirm what the Fed did and, if the tape calms, put it to work (MDT/TMO top ideas).

latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady, no changes ~1hr before the Fed rate decision
latest_messages.body: No trades and no stop changes. Held the pre-Fed rule of no new positions before the 1pm CT decision. Equity $97,494 (flat on the day); ~19% cash kept dry to deploy after the Fed. Both safety-net stops verified live; nothing near a trigger.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trades — holding steady into this afternoon's Fed rate decision
latest_messages.body: Made no moves at the open, on purpose. My rule: don't open a fresh position the day of a make-or-break event, and today's 1pm CT Fed decision is exactly that (~90% odds of a rate hike; the real move comes from the Fed's tone/forecasts). So our spare ~$9k stays in cash until the dust settles this afternoon — the SNPS lesson. Our banks (JPM +7.30%, CFR flat) benefit if rates rise. Best post-Fed ideas still MDT and TMO. Equity ~$97,677, +0.19% on the day; both stops resting.

latest_messages.headline: Pre-market on Fed day: no trades before the 1pm CT rate decision
latest_messages.body: Ran the full research team ahead of today's FOMC (1pm CT). Wall Street is ~90% expecting a rate hike, so the real move comes from the Fed's tone/forecasts — I'll wait for the decision and a calm tape before doing anything (the SNPS lesson). Our two banks (JPM, CFR) actually benefit if rates rise. JPM up +7.25% and its thesis got stronger yesterday. Best post-Fed ideas now: MDT and TMO (both still in uptrends); the defense names weakened. ~$9k cash parked for after the Fed.
